conviction_note: Fundamentals lean positive: peers that spoke after TXN's 22 July call guided +7-8% sequential, Taiwan analog series were still rising in September, and the published Q4 consensus (~$5.68-5.74B, about -3% q/q) looks stale against that. Against this, TXN sold its July beat-and-raise (-3.1%), NXP sold its beat (-5.5%), the stock has gone nowhere since July and the 25d skew pays +9.7 vol points for downside. So p_up sits only slightly above 50 (53) on an abs move of 7.5 (implied 6.78, median reaction 7.52, and a Q4 guide is always new), giving +0.45. Findings sum to +0.7. The gap between the two is the reaction-function discount, not an inconsistency.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue ~$5.91B / adj EPS ~$2.40-2.42 (iTiger 2026-10-15 https://www.itiger.com/news/1199935814 ; Hudson Labs 2026-10-05 https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/texas-instruments-q3-2026-earnings-preview-txn-results ; Earnings Whispers consensus $2.40, whisper $2.46, rev $5.93B https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/TXN), which equals the company guide midpoint ($5.65-6.15B, EPS $2.23-2.57). Q4 2026 bar: Benzinga snippet $5.68B / $2.26 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TXN/earnings-forecasts, undated, snippet_only) and FY2026 revenue consensus $21.91B / EPS $8.49 on stockanalysis.com (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/txn/forecast/), which less Q1 $4.8B + Q2 $5.463B + Q3 $5.91B implies Q4 ~$5.74B. The two Q4 sources roughly agree (-3% to -4% q/q). The buy-side Q4 bar is unsourced and probably higher.
positioning_check: Short interest 20.44m shares, 2.25% of float, 3.2 days to cover, up 3.5% from the prior settlement, record date 2026-09-30, published 2026-10-09 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/TXN/short-interest/). Not a crowded short. 25d skew is +9.67 vol points (downside paid) and front-expiry put/call OI is 0.47 (call-heavy OI). The event-implied move is 6.78%. Run-up is +2.6% over 5 days and +5.65% over 20 days. Spot is 13.3% below the 52-week high (~$334, set around June-July) and roughly back at the level after the July print ($277 open / $294 prior close on 2026-07-23).

findings.finding: Independent Taiwan analog series kept rising after TXN last spoke on 22 July. Silergy (6415, a China-centric power-analog peer) reported September revenue of NT$2.511bn, +3.9% m/m and +50.7% y/y, on 8 Oct. Its Q3 total is NT$7.27bn (YTD Sep 18.141bn less H1 10.869bn) against a H1 quarterly average of ~NT$5.43bn. That is consistent with TXN printing in the upper half of its $5.65-6.15B guide rather than at the $5.91B consensus midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $5.46B vs $5.24-5.25B consensus (~+4%) with an above-seasonal guide, and the stock fell -3.1% close to close (baseline; https://www.tradingpedia.com/2026/07/23/texas-instruments-stock-drops-despite-upbeat-forecast/). Q1 2026 beat-and-raise: +19.4%. The reported-quarter beat alone has not been paid reliably.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus still sits exactly on the guide midpoint ($5.91B), so the street has not marked Q3 to the upper half. A Taiwanese monthly filing in Chinese is not in the US preview copy. The whisper ($2.46 vs $2.40) shows the buy-side expects some beat, and a beat inside the guided range is what the company told the market to expect, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Separate source: WT Microelectronics (distributor) reportedly posted a record September at about NT$215.9bn, +9% m/m (snippet_only, LinkedIn repost: https://tr.linkedin.com/in/cem-urgup-8557a724). WPG August revenue was +80.5% y/y (https://www.wpgholdings.com/news/detail/en/revenue/26042). These are proxies, not TXN numbers. TXN's China exposure is 22% of revenue by HQ (10-Q).

findings.finding: The published Q4 2026 bar (~$5.68-5.74B, about -3% q/q from a $5.91B Q3) looks stale against peers that guided after TXN last spoke. ADI (19 Aug) printed $4.02B against a $3.9B guide and guided Aug-Oct to $4.2-4.4B vs $4.08B consensus, with its CFO saying demand 'continued to strengthen ... throughout the third quarter'. Microchip (6 Aug) guided the Sep quarter +8% q/q with book-to-bill 'well above 1'. TXN itself said price increases execute in Q3 and continue into Q4. A Q4 guide midpoint near flat (~$5.9-6.0B) would beat the published bar by 3-5%. TXN's own Q4 habit is -5% to -7% (e.g. Q4 2025 guide midpoint $4.40B vs Q3 2025 $4.74B), so the published bar already assumes above-seasonal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide surprises dominate this name. Apr 2026, strong Q2 guide: +19.4%. Jan 2026: +9.9%. Jul 2026, Q3 guide above the $5.61B consensus: -3.1% (profit-taking after a ~70% YTD run). Oct 2025, weak Q4 guide: -5.6%. Jul 2025: -13.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had priced a flat-to-up Q4, the published Q4 consensus would sit near $5.9-6.0B rather than $5.68-5.74B, and the stock would not still be at its post-July level ($288 vs a $277 open on 23 Jul) while peers re-rated on raises. The skew (+9.7 downside) says the options market leans to a disappointing guide or a 'peak cycle' read, so the sign is against the skew. The reason the market may be wrong: the counterparties' own guides (ADI +7%, MCHP +8%) plus a pricing tailwind landing in Q4 are company-level numbers, not inference. The buy-side bar is unsourced and likely above the published one, so the size stays well below the implied move.
findings.independence: Microchip guide: https://quartr.com/events/microchip-technology-inc-mchp-q1-2027_3etrCKBt (2026-08-06). NXP Q3 guide raised to ~$3.75B midpoint, but the stock fell 5.5% (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nxp-semiconductors-nasdaqnxpi-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-07-28/). TXN pricing commentary: Hudson Labs preview (2026-10-05). Q4 bar: Benzinga snippet and the stockanalysis FY figure. Different documents, one thesis.

findings.finding: Price increases are hitting the P&L for the first time this cycle: TXN said pricing was flat in H1 and increases execute customer by customer in Q3 into Q4 and 2027, mainly in Analog (82% of Q2 revenue at $4.365B). With fabs under-loaded (inventory 196 days, 'loadings adjusted further in Q3'), gross margin is set for upside against the 61.8% Q3 consensus (Q2 printed ~61.4%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 gross margin rose ~300-340bp q/q and EPS beat by ~11%, yet the stock fell -3.1%. Margin beats have not been paid on their own.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: consensus GM already assumes +40bp q/q and the EPS whisper sits $0.06 above consensus. What is not visible is the size of the price uplift, which TXN has not quantified. Sized small and mostly inside the guided EPS range.
findings.independence: ADI raised prices again from 13 Sep 2026 (TrendForce, https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/08/13/news-adi-reportedly-set-to-raise-prices-again-on-september-with-military-chips-facing-up-to-30-hike/), which shows industry-wide pricing power. Q2 GM is from TXN's 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000152/txn-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: Reaction function and positioning: TXN and its closest peer both sold beat-and-raise prints this cycle (TXN -3.1% on 22 Jul, NXP -5.5% on 28 Jul). TXN has gone sideways since July despite peer raises. The option market pays +9.67 vol points for 25d puts over calls, and short interest rose 3.5% to 2.25% of float (3.2 days) into the print. A good print with a merely in-line or seasonal Q4 guide is likely sold again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Of the last 7 prints, 3 rose. Both 2025 Q3 (-5.6%) and 2026 Q2 (-3.1%) fell despite fundamentally fine quarters.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the priced side, filed as the counterweight. The skew is the market's own statement, and the risk is that the bull findings above are what the buy-side already holds (whisper above consensus, 8 of 9 directional analyst calls bullish per iTiger). It is not a crowded short (2.25%), so there is no squeeze mechanism to shrink it further.
findings.independence: Short interest: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/TXN/short-interest/ (2026-09-30 record). NXP reaction: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nxp-semiconductors-nasdaqnxpi-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-07-28/. Skew is from the sealed baseline.

findings.finding: On 17 Sep 2026 TXN pre-announced a 7% dividend increase ($1.42 to $1.52 quarterly), larger than last year's ~4% step ($1.36 to $1.42). It is subject to the board's October meeting and framed as returning all FCF over time, a signal of management's FCF confidence with capex tracking the low end of $2-3B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction attributable to the dividend line. FCF-per-share commentary was part of the Apr 2026 +19.4% print.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since it was public on 17 Sep. The formal declaration at the October board meeting likely comes with the release and confirms it. Filed small because a larger raise than last year is a management tell on Q4 cash.
findings.independence: Capex tracking the low end and FCF/share above the $8 target: Hudson Labs preview (2026-10-05). Shares the FCF thesis with nothing else in this file.

findings.finding: Personal electronics is constrained by memory. TXN guided only modest Q3 sequential growth in that segment because of memory shortages, and NXP said mobile would decline y/y in Q3 on component constraints. This caps one end market (roughly a mid-teens share of revenue) into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated history. Net of the rest of the company, industrial (+30% y/y), data center (2x y/y) and auto (mid-teens) dominate the mix, so this segment drag is small.
findings.why_not_priced: Company-disclosed, so mostly priced. Filed because a Q4 guide comment extending the memory constraint would trim the above-seasonal case.
findings.independence: NXP Q3 commentary on mobile constraints: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nxp-semiconductors-nasdaqnxpi-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-07-28/

findings.finding: This is the first earnings call with Julie Knecht as CFO (effective 1 Aug 2026, succeeding the retiring Rafael Lizardi), and therefore her first Q4 guide. A first-time CFO guide carries some risk of a conservative midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history for this CFO. The 8-K of 2026-06-02 (item 5.02) documents the transition.
findings.why_not_priced: The transition is public. The guide-conservatism effect is an inference with no TXN-specific evidence, so it is filed small.
findings.independence: EDGAR 8-K item 5.02 dated 2026-06-02 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000097476&type=8-K). Same fact, no independent pointer to the direction.

outside_window.finding: China MOFCOM anti-dumping probe into US analog interface and gate-driver ICs (TXN named). It opened 2025-09-13, was normally due by 2026-09-13 and is extendable by six months to ~2027-03-13. No preliminary or final determination was found in search. China was 22% of TXN Q2 revenue by HQ. A ruling is not dated inside the window. Call commentary could touch it, but no in-window catalyst is identified.

Silicon Labs acquisition ($231/sh cash, ~$7.5B EV). SLAB holders approved it on 2026-04-30, and TXN signed a $5B 364-day delayed-draw term loan in June 2026, undrawn and conditional on closing. Close is expected H1 2027. The financing buys a strategic acquisition with $450m targeted synergies, not distress, so it is signed neutral to slightly positive and resolves after the window.

baseline_tension: The fundamental evidence (peer guides, Taiwan monthly series, pricing) points up and cuts against the +9.7 put skew. The modest +5.65% 20-day run-up and a stock flat since the July sell-the-beat say the market is sceptical of cycle durability, not unaware of the strength. So p_up is held at 53, not higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guided range): the Taiwan-series / Q3 upper-half finding lands inside the $5.65-6.15B guide, so it was cut from +0.8 to +0.4.

Rules 1 and 7 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; sign against a strong skew): the Q4-guide finding was cut from +1.5 to +1.2 because TXN sold its July beat-and-raise and the 25d skew is +9.7; why_not_priced now states explicitly why the options market may be wrong (counterparty guides of +7-8% vs a -3% published Q4 bar). p_up was moved from 54 to 53.
Rule 6 again: pricing/GM finding cut from +0.4 to +0.3 because it is largely inside the guided EPS range.
Dividend finding cut from +0.2 to +0.1 because it has been public since 17 Sep.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): personal-electronics drag cut from -0.3 to -0.2, since industrial, data center and auto dominate the mix.
Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the CFO-conservatism inference was cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the Silicon Labs $5B delayed-draw term loan funds an acquisition and is signed neutral; it was already in outside_window and nothing changed.
Rule 7 (short interest before a negative): checked (2.25%, 3.2 days, not crowded); the positioning negative stays at -1.0.
